newsitem.title: UK: Airbus wins $2 bln order for new jet from Virgin.
newsitem.headline: Airbus wins $2 bln order for new jet from Virgin.

text.p: British airline Virgin Atlantic Airways announced a two billion dollar deal on Friday to order a fleet of new A340-600 widebody jets from Europe's Airbus Industrie consortium.

The order makes Virgin the first customer for the bigger 375-seat version of the four-engine longhaul aircraft, which Airbus launched at the Paris Airshow in June. First delivery will be in the year 2002.
Virgin also said it was ordering two more of the existing A340-300 jets for delivery next year. Altogether the deal was valued at around $2.5 billion, industry sources said.
Airbus wins $2 bln order for new jet from Virgin

Virgin said it plans to fit out the new A340-600 aircraft as two-deck aircraft with the lower deck featuring bedrooms for Upper Class passengers as well as showers, a bar and exercise and massage rooms.
"The layout will be stunning," said a spokesman for the airline.

Currently Virgin operates 20 aircraft, including eight Airbus A340-300s, five Boeing 747-400s and an Airbus A320 narrow-body jet and six older generation 747s, which will be phased out with the arrival of the new aircraft.
The current A340-300 seats around 280 passengers in three-class configuration.

Airbus has already said it expects to spend $2.5 billion developing the new 600 version and a longer range 500 version of the A340, to cut into rival Boeing Co's monopoly of the high capacity long range sector of the market with its 777 and 747-400 'jumbo' jets.
The A340-600 will have a range of 7,500 nautical miles while the 500 version which will fly 313 passengers up to 8,300 nautical miles, making it the longest range airliner in the world.

The new aircraft will be powered by a new version of Rolls-Royce Plc's Trent engines under a special development deal between the British engine manufacturer and Airbus which was also announced in June.
Airbus head of sales John Leahy told reporters at the Paris air show that the company was looking to sell the new A340-500 and A340-600s for around $140 and $150 million apiece.
A spokesman for Virgin said the airline will lease the aircraft but declined to put a value on the order. "All I can say is that we got a very good deal," he said.
It was also confirmed on Friday that Air Canada has also decided to become a launch customer by ordering five A340-600 and A340-500s next March.
